PC: You should see this patient right away and perform a head-to-toe physical exam to evaluate for any possible sources of infection.
In addition, this patient merits broad-spectrum antibiotics and cultures looking for potential source of infection.
For laboratory evaluation, this would include CBC, LFTs, 2 sets of blood cultures from peripheral veins and/or any catheters, urinalysis and urine culture, and consideration of chest X-ray.
For treatment, good broad-spectrum antibiotics would include piperacillin/tazobactam or cefepime (though cefepime will not cover anaerobes well).
If there is concern for Gram positive infection, or if the patient is hemodynamically unstable, you should also add on vancomycin for MRSA coverage.
While in most cases no clear source for the infection is found, prompt antibiotics and supportive care (e.g. fluids) are important to prevent patient from decompensating.
